abstract.p: We introduce GREEKBARBENCH, a benchmark that evaluates LLMs on legal questions across five different legal areas from the Greek Bar exams, requiring citations to statutory articles and case facts. To tackle the challenges of free-text evaluation, we propose a threedimensional scoring system combined with an LLM-as-a-judge approach. We also develop a meta-evaluation benchmark to assess the correlation between LLM-judges and human expert evaluations, revealing that simple, span-based rubrics improve their alignment. Our extensive evaluation of 13 proprietary and open-weight LLMs shows that even though the top models exhibit impressive performance, they remain susceptible to critical errors, most notably a failure to identify the correct statutory articles.
